open_obligations: Note that Wu et al.'s levels are subtasks of one policy, not separately trained assistants as in recursive reward modeling.
Check whether the compounding was measured quantitatively or observed qualitatively.
Check whether any self-correcting mechanism of the kind Leike et al. suggest was tried.
out.other_title: Do errors accumulate across levels of recursive reward modeling?
out.rationale: Leike et al. pose whether mistakes of narrower agents lead to larger mistakes higher up. Wu et al. report that policy errors at lower levels compound at each composition task, leading to large top-level errors, and that training on the full tree did not improve performance; their hierarchy is a fixed summarisation tree, not a chain of assistant agents training stronger agents.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether errors at lower levels of a recursive human-feedback hierarchy compound upward, for recursive book summarisation

text: The authors state that in general policy errors at lower levels compound at each composition task, leading to large errors on the top-level task, and that auto-induced distributional shift may make training significantly harder; curriculum and node sampling were chosen ad hoc. Training on the full tree of tasks did not improve performance, and they leave investigation to future work.
title: Errors compound up the tree; training on higher-height tasks may be difficult
